author: barry
body: Same capacitor went bad in my KitchenAid side-by-side built in refrigerator. My symptoms were the display inside the frig that shows the actual temp and set temp would not stay on. On power-up, all the display lights would flash on for a few seconds then turn off. Replacing the 220uf cap on the control board solved the problem. Thanks for taking the time to write this up. It was helpful.

author: Federico Hatoum
body: I'm glad my post helped you resolve the problem with your refrigerator, and thank you for taking the time to post a comment.

author: Darcy
body: Same problem happened with my Kitchenaid side by side. My fridge started beeping occasionally and ultimately the compressor started to cut out intermittently. Thanks to you and Steve Jenkins I was able to identify that the same capacitor on the control board had failed. I was a bit intimidated by the delicate soldering so I took mine to a computer repair shop. 30 minutes and $30 later - problem is fixed. Fridge is running like new.

author: Evelyn Guo
body:
Hi Federico,

I think I am experiencing the same problem, may I ask where did you buy the new capacitor?

author: Federico Hatoum
body:
Hi Evelyn,

I had spare capacitors from other projects. However, you can buy capacitors online.

author: Palisandr
body:
Thank you very much for the post! Exactly the same happened to my Kitchenaid side-by-side KSSC42FTS03 model. Chirping sound, identified the same bulging capacitor. Fortunately, I have an elderly friend, who knows what hot iron and soldering is and he had the needed capacitor (replaced the bad one with 220nF, 50V, 105C).

Great, helpful post. Thank again.

author: Federico Hatoum
body: You're welcome! Glad you found the post useful.
